facts.claim: A Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) is a DFAT document issued in support of an intended marriage overseas, because local authorities may ask you to prove you are not already married. DFAT issues CNIs through Australian Passport Offices across Australia, through Australian embassies, high commissions and consulates overseas, and by mail.
facts.publisher: Smartraveller (DFAT), How to get a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage
facts.reused_from: malta-wedding B F-100 / destination-wedding-in-vietnam B F-100 (getting-married-in-france B, checked 2026-11-16)

facts.claim: At least one person applying for the CNI must be an Australian citizen or permanent resident. Supporting documents: Australian citizen, a valid Australian passport; permanent resident, a valid foreign passport with evidence of permanent residence; foreign citizen partner, a valid foreign passport or photo ID; divorced, a Divorce Certificate; widowed, the deceased partner's Death Certificate. Originals or certified true copies; non-English documents need a professional English translation.
facts.publisher: Smartraveller (DFAT), How to get a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage

facts.claim: How to apply for a CNI through DFAT: complete the CNI application form, signing it only in front of an authorised witness (in Australia a Justice of the Peace, or an Australian Passports official at your appointment; overseas a consular official). If the overseas authority wants documents legalised, also complete a Document Legalisation Request Form. Submit by mail or in person and pay on submission. Incomplete applications are not processed. DFAT advises checking whether the CNI must be issued in the country of marriage, in which case the Australian embassy there can issue it.
facts.publisher: Smartraveller (DFAT), How to get a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage
facts.use_note: Australia has no embassy or high commission in Jamaica (F-117), so the simplest route is DFAT in Australia before departure. Whether Jamaica wants a CNI at all, and apostilled, is a Jamaica-side question (N-100).

facts.claim: DFAT notarial fees from 1 January 2026, in Australian dollars: Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage AUD 181; document legalisation by Apostille AUD 105. Fees rise with CPI on 1 January each year.
facts.use_note: Write 'From AUD 181 per CNI (2026 fee)' and 'From AUD 105 per apostille (2026 fee)'. Matches the Port of Spain fee table read today (F-119). Re-check after 1 January 2027.

facts.claim: DFAT does not publish a fixed processing time for legalisation: 'Processing times vary', with delays at the end of the school year and during peak holiday periods, when a request is incomplete or unpaid, or when DFAT must contact the document's issuing authority.
facts.publisher: Smartraveller (DFAT), How to get your documents legalised

facts.claim: You cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia. Australia does not recognise overseas marriages where either person was already married, not old enough, too closely related, or forced to marry. A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, but may not be usable as proof of a name change; check with your state or territory BDM registry. Smartraveller suggests talking to a lawyer to confirm an overseas certificate is valid in Australia.

The Attorney-General's Department says overseas marriages cannot be performed by an Australian-authorised marriage celebrant or registered in Australia, and an overseas marriage is generally recognised in Australia if it was valid in the overseas country and would have been valid here. Some states and territories do not accept overseas marriage certificates for a change of name. Legal basis: Marriage Act 1961, Part VA (recognition of foreign marriages).
facts.use_note: Cite Part VA by name only; section text not read.

facts.claim: Passport name change after marriage: for a new passport you must link the new name to your Australian birth or citizenship certificate with an Australian RBDM marriage certificate, registered relationship certificate, or RBDM name change certificate. The Passport Office always requires an RBDM name change certificate if you were born in Australia and married overseas. Foreign certificates are accepted only if you cannot get an Australian equivalent, must be legalised, and non-English documents must be translated in full by an approved translation service.
facts.publisher: Australian Passport Office, Change of name or gender
facts.use_note: An Australian-born spouse married in Jamaica first registers a change of name with their state BDM before getting a passport in the new name. Jamaica's certificates are in English, so no translation step is expected, but that is not confirmed from an official page (N-102).

facts.claim: NSW Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages: a person legally married in Australia can take their spouse's family name without registering a change of name (the exemption is worded for marriages in Australia). Foreign documents not in English must be translated in full and stamped by a NAATI-accredited translator, with copies of the original and the translation.
facts.publisher: NSW Government, Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages
facts.use_note: NSW only; other states not checked.

facts.claim: If you change your family name because of marriage, you can choose to get a new passport or keep using your current one, and the Australian Passport Office recommends booking travel in the name that is in your passport.
facts.use_note: Book the Jamaica flights and honeymoon in the name on the passport you will carry.

facts.claim: Smartraveller's essentials checklist says to confirm your passport is valid for at least 6 months beyond the end of your trip; some countries and some airlines apply a six-month validity rule, it can apply when transiting, and getting it wrong can mean being stranded.
facts.use_note: Jamaica page gives only the generic 'many countries' note (F-121). Safe wording: 'check your passport is valid for at least 6 months beyond your trip'.

facts.claim: Allow at least 6 weeks to get a passport; where possible, don't book flights without a valid passport; faster processing may be available for urgent travel at an extra fee.

Legal at home, celebration abroad: Australia has no marriage licence; the formal step is giving a Notice of Intended Marriage (NOIM) to an authorised celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding. You do not have to be an Australian citizen or permanent resident to marry in Australia. Since 12 June 2024 the NOIM can be witnessed remotely by audio-visual link, and a couple outside Australia can complete it with an authorised witness overseas (such as an Australian consular officer or a notary public, not a celebrant).
facts.reused_from: malta-wedding B F-112 (getting-married-in-france B F-112, originally marriage-licence-requirements A F-001 to F-005)

facts.claim: Since 12 June 2024 the authorised celebrant must meet separately and in person with each party before the marriage, and must be physically present to solemnise it, together with the couple and 2 witnesses over 18. There are no video-link weddings.
facts.use_note: The Australian legal ceremony cannot be done from Jamaica by video.

facts.claim: After an Australian ceremony the celebrant must submit the NOIM, the Declaration of No Legal Impediment and the Official Certificate of Marriage to the BDM registry in the state or territory where the marriage took place within 14 days.
facts.publisher: Attorney-General's Department, Notice of Intended Marriage form
facts.use_note: Benefit of the home route: an Australian BDM certificate, which the Passport Office accepts directly (F-107).

facts.claim: HCCH status table for the 1961 Apostille Convention (last update 30 June 2026): Jamaica acceded on 2 November 2020 and the Convention entered into force for Jamaica on 3 July 2021 (type A, accession, no objection marker). Australia acceded on 11 July 1994 with entry into force on 16 March 1995. Both are Contracting Parties, so an Australian public document for use in Jamaica is legalised by apostille rather than consular legalisation.
facts.publisher: Hague Conference on Private International Law (HCCH), Apostille Convention status table
facts.use_note: Apostille from DFAT (From AUD 105 per document, 2026 fee, F-103). Which Australian documents Jamaica's registering authority wants apostilled is a Jamaica-side question (N-100). Older guides that describe Jamaican consular legalisation predate July 2021.

facts.claim: Smartraveller's overall advice for Jamaica is 'Exercise a high degree of caution' due to the threat of violent crime (still current at 17 November 2026; updated 4 November 2026). Hotspots for violent crime include parts of Kingston, St Catherine, Montego Bay and May Pen. Smartraveller advises arranging airport transport in advance, using established tour operators or taxis authorised by the Jamaican United Travellers' Association (JUTA), avoiding public transport, avoiding beaches at night and never accepting food or drink from strangers, including in resorts.
facts.use_note: Level 2 of 4 (yellow). State it plainly and link the page; useful for guest transfers (pre-booked transport). Levels can change at short notice.

facts.claim: Smartraveller Jamaica: Australia has a consulate in Kingston headed by an honorary consul, which provides limited consular services and conducts passport interviews (80-82 Second Street, Port Bustamante, Kingston 13; phone +1 876 361 1332). Full consular assistance comes from the Australian High Commission in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago (18 Herbert Street, St Clair, Port of Spain; phone +1 868 235 7950; email ahc.portofspain@dfat.gov.au; website trinidadandtobago.highcommission.gov.au). The 24-hour Consular Emergency Centre is +61 2 6261 3305 from overseas or 1300 555 135 in Australia.
facts.use_note: Do not publish the honorary consul's personal email; link the Smartraveller page instead. Smartraveller does not say the Kingston honorary consulate offers notarial or CNI services.

facts.claim: Australian High Commission, Port of Spain: the High Commissioner to Trinidad and Tobago is also accredited to Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Haiti, Jamaica, St Kitts and Nevis, St Lucia, St Vincent and the Grenadines, Suriname and The Bahamas. The High Commission is open 8am to 4:30pm Monday to Friday, except listed public holidays, and lists an honorary consulate in Kingston, Jamaica.
facts.publisher: Australian High Commission Trinidad and Tobago (DFAT), About us
facts.use_note: Answers 'which Australian mission covers Jamaica': the Australian High Commission in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago.

facts.claim: Australian High Commission, Port of Spain notarial services: it provides a limited range of notarial services for Australian citizens, Australian permanent residents, and other nationalities where documents are for use in Australia; contact the High Commission to book. Its fee table (as at 1 November 2026) lists preparation and issue of a certificate of no impediment to marriage at USD 127 / AUD 181 / TTD 836, an Apostille certificate at USD 74 / AUD 105 / TTD 485, an Authentication certificate at the same USD 74 / AUD 105 / TTD 485, and witnessing a signature at USD 63 / AUD 90 / TTD 416.
facts.publisher: Australian High Commission Trinidad and Tobago (DFAT), Notarial services
facts.use_note: The fee table shows the High Commission can issue a CNI, but the page gives no CNI procedure, no mail option and nothing on serving clients located in Jamaica; it would likely mean contacting or travelling to Port of Spain. Hence medium. Recommend applying through DFAT in Australia before travel (F-102); couples already in the Caribbean should contact ahc.portofspain@dfat.gov.au. Also answers N-103 in the Vietnam batch: the authentication fee equals the apostille fee (AUD 105) at this post.

facts.claim: Smartraveller Jamaica entry: Australians don't need a visa to enter Jamaica for tourism if staying less than 6 months, or for business if staying less than 30 days; in other situations apply for a visa through a Jamaican embassy or consulate. All travellers must complete the free Immigration/Customs C5 Form online before arrival via the Government of Jamaica Passport Immigration Citizenship Agency (PICA) website, enterjamaica.com. Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice; contact a Jamaican embassy and the Jamaica Customs Agency for details.
facts.use_note: A wedding trip is a tourism visit; do not present 'wedding' as a named visa category. Applies to the couple and every Australian guest. enterjamaica.com was not read directly; cite Smartraveller.

facts.claim: Smartraveller Jamaica: you need a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Jamaica if you arrive from or transit through a country where yellow fever is widespread; travellers who have been in an Ebola-affected country in the last 21 days face enhanced health screening on arrival. If travelling through the US, including Hawaii or another US point of entry, you must meet US entry and transit requirements. Passport note: many countries require your passport to be valid for at least 6 months before entering or departing, including for transit; the Australian Government does not make these rules.
facts.use_note: Passport wording is generic, not a Jamaica-specific six-month rule; do not state one as fact. The US transit point matters because many routes from Australia connect through the US; tell guests to check US transit rules (ESTA or visa) early. Specific flight routes not researched here.

facts.claim: Smartraveller Jamaica: the Caribbean hurricane season is from June to November, and tropical storms and hurricanes can occur in other months. Landslides, mudslides and flooding can also occur, and severe weather can delay or suspend flights, affect road travel and disrupt water, electricity and communications. If travelling during hurricane season, check whether severe weather has affected tourist services. The risk of insect-borne illnesses such as dengue and chikungunya increases in the wet season from June to December.
facts.use_note: Only climate statements from an approved official source. December to May is outside hurricane season, but do not call it 'dry season' or give temperatures: the Meteorological Service of Jamaica was not read (N-104). Recommend travel insurance and a weather buffer for June to November dates.

facts.claim: Smartraveller Jamaica local law: same-sex relationships are illegal and aren't widely accepted; Jamaican law prohibits sexual acts between people of the same sex, with sentences of up to 10 years, though authorities rarely enforce the law, and there are continued reports of serious discrimination and abuse against LGBTQIA+ people. Jamaica recognises dual nationality. It is illegal to swear, be nude in public, or buy, sell or wear camouflage-style clothing.
facts.use_note: Important for an inclusive brand: a same-sex couple cannot have a legal wedding in Jamaica and faces real safety risk; say so plainly and point to the legal-at-home route (F-112). Whether Jamaican law permits same-sex marriage was not read on a Jamaican source (N-100); Smartraveller states the relationship law only. Camouflage note is useful for guest packing lists.

facts.claim: Smartraveller Jamaica money and medical: the local currency is the Jamaican dollar (JMD) and you must declare all currency on arrival, covering all forms of currency, not only cash. ATMs aren't widely available outside Kingston and Montego Bay. Medical treatment costs can be high, hospitals may require cash or a credit card imprint before treatment, and serious cases may need evacuation to Miami; get comprehensive travel insurance that covers medical evacuation.
facts.use_note: Optional travel-prep line. Currency declaration matters for couples carrying vendor payments in cash.

legal.summary: DFAT issues CNIs in Australia, by mail and through overseas missions. Confirm the current CNI process with DFAT.

Australia has no resident embassy or high commission in Jamaica; the Australian High Commission in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago, is accredited to Jamaica. An honorary consul in Kingston gives limited consular services and passport interviews. Confirm with the High Commission (ahc.portofspain@dfat.gov.au).

The Port of Spain High Commission lists a CNI fee (AUD 181, USD 127 or TTD 836 as at 1 November 2026), so it can issue CNIs, but publishes no procedure for applicants in Jamaica. Confirm with the High Commission or apply through DFAT in Australia.

Both parties to the Apostille Convention (Jamaica since 3 July 2021, Australia since 16 March 1995): Australian documents for Jamaica are apostilled by DFAT. Which documents need an apostille is confirmed with Jamaica's registering authority (Registrar General's Department or Ministry responsible for marriage licences; batch A).

No Australian registration of overseas marriages; generally recognised if valid in Jamaica and would be valid in Australia (Marriage Act 1961, Part VA). Confirm with DFAT, a lawyer, or your state BDM registry for name change use.
Passport in married name: an Australian-born spouse married overseas needs an RBDM name change certificate. Confirm with the Australian Passport Office and the state BDM registry.
Legal at home route: NOIM to an authorised celebrant 1 to 18 months ahead; celebrant physically present. Confirm with the Attorney-General's Department guidance and your celebrant.
